The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
The Story of the Mansion of Guttila 1.
The Story of the Mansion of the Giver of the Best Cloth “With seven strings, most sweetly sounding...”
I recited the *Ramaṇeyya* hymn;
he challenged me in the arena,
saying, “Become my refuge, O Kosiya!”
“I am your refuge; I am the one who honors the teacher.
Your disciple shall not defeat you.”
“O teacher of my pupil, you are victorious!
[The deity replied: “With a most excellent complexion, O deity, you stand there;”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs,
by what cause do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those riches that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance illuminates all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When asked the question,
she explained it as the fruit of that specific deed:
"I was a woman who gave the most excellent cloth."
She is preeminent among men and women;
thus, as a giver of what is lovely and pleasing,
she attains and dwells in a celestial realm.
Behold my celestial mansion!
I am a nymph of lovely form; I am the mistress of a thousand nymphs.
Behold, Pavarā, the ripening of merits!
It is because of that my complexion is such as this,
and it is because of that I prosper here.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is dear to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds; because of that,
my majestic power blazes forth in this way,
and my complexion illuminates all directions."
(Immediately following, the *Caturavimāna* should be expanded in detail just as the *Vatthadāyikāvimāna* was.

12. The Mansion of Her Who Gave Molasses "With a most excellent complexion... [as before] ... [omitted] ... "Where have you come from? "O King, I am not a human being; I am a deva dwelling in a mansion. Because I gave molasses to the Buddha Kassapa, I have been reborn here in this celestial mansion. "How long is the lifespan of those who dwell in this mansion? "For a full ten thousand years, O Great King, they shall remain here in bliss. "I wish to go there, O deva; please take me with you. "It is not possible for me to take you there, O Great King. However, if you perform meritorious deeds, you will be reborn there yourself. "By what means, O deva, may I be reborn in that same place?
